payload.name: Resolve deictic time expressions during extraction
payload.description: When a user message states an event happened or an item was received using only a relative time word (yesterday, today, last week, N days ago), during extraction resolve it with the message timestamp and create an event memory.
content: During extraction, if a user message states a concrete event (e.g., receiving/being given something, an occurrence) and gives only a deictic time word such as 'yesterday', 'today', 'this morning', or 'N days ago', compute the absolute date using the message's occurred_at timestamp and create an event candidate (memory kind: event) with that date and the original evidence.

Do not create such a candidate when the statement is just an object mention without an event verb, or when the message already provides an absolute date; in the latter case keep normal extraction with the stated date.
If no occurred_at timestamp is available for the message, do not guess a date; skip the deictic resolution and continue with base extraction.

solves: Construction extraction sometimes drops facts whose only temporal anchor is a relative expression such as 'yesterday', leaving later 'when did X happen' questions unanswerable. This Skill applies when a user message names an event (e.g., receiving a letter) and gives only a deictic time; it resolves that time from the message timestamp and creates an event memory. It must not apply when the text already contains an absolute date or when no usable message timestamp exists, because the base resolution rule already covers those cases.
